meta.description: Human-reviewed contributor queue. The bot reads this file and nothing else. Every entry is reviewed in a normal pull request, which is the point: an agent that decides at runtime what to build will duplicate, hallucinate, and file issues nobody can action.
notes: status: backlog    -> not eligible to be filed
status: ready      -> eligible; the bot may file it when the cap allows
status: filed      -> the bot created it; the marker lives in the issue body
status: shipped    -> the bot may comment + close its own issue, naming the release
Only entries with status=ready AND a complete body are ever filed.

items.title: docs: document the doctor and brain commands that already exist
items.body:
## Context

`package.json` already ships `doctor` (`node scripts/setup.js --check`) and `brain` (`node scripts/braincheck.js`), and the README mentions neither. A newcomer with a misconfigured model has no documented way to diagnose it.

## What to change

- `README.md`: after the install block, add `npm run doctor` and `npm run brain`, one line each on what they check.
- `docs/GUIDE.md`: add a "When something is wrong" subsection pointing at both.

Docs only; do not touch `src/` or `scripts/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run doctor` appears in `README.md` and `docs/GUIDE.md`
- [ ] Both are described from real output you ran yourself
- [ ] `node --test` still passes

## How to verify

```bash
node scripts/setup.js --check
node scripts/braincheck.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. The "Install it in two commands" block near the top of `README.md`.
2. The configuration section of `docs/GUIDE.md`.

## Time estimate

~1-2 hours.

items.title: test(security): prove resolveInWorkspace() refuses a symlink escape
items.body:
## Context

`src/tools.js:90` defines `resolveInWorkspace()`, and the README makes a security claim about it: files are confined to `PINCH_WORKSPACE` through `realpath()`, so a symlink cannot walk out. That claim has no targeted regression test.

Run the case by hand first. If the guard does **not** hold, stop and report it privately per `SECURITY.md` instead of opening a public PR.

## What to change

- `test/hardening.test.js`: add a test that creates a temp workspace, plants a symlink pointing outside it, and asserts `resolveInWorkspace()` refuses the path.
- Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. No new dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test fails if `realpath()` confinement is removed (check by patching temporarily, then revert)
- [ ] Temp directory cleaned up in a `finally` block
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24 and 26
- [ ] Test name states the guarantee, not the implementation

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/hardening.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/tools.js:90` - `resolveInWorkspace()`, about 30 lines.
2. `test/hardening.test.js` - copy the setup/teardown pattern from the nearest case.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: test(cli): cover --version and an unknown verb in a smoke test
items.body:
## Context

`bin/pinch.js` is the entry point every user touches, and `scripts/growth.js` already carries a CLI-drift collector because promised verbs have drifted from implemented ones before. There is still no test that runs the CLI and asserts `--version` and an unknown verb behave sanely.

## What to change

- `test/cli.test.js` (new): via `node:child_process` `execFile` (argv array, never a shell string),
  1. `--version` exits 0 and prints the `package.json` version;
  2. an unknown verb exits non-zero or prints usage - assert whichever it does today and say which in the name;
  3. `help` prints a usage line containing a real verb.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No hard-coded version string; read it from `package.json`
- [ ] `execFile` with an argv array
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24, 26
- [ ] `node --test` still fully green

## How to verify

```bash
node bin/pinch.js --version
node bin/pinch.js help
node bin/pinch.js nope; echo "exit=$?"
node --test test/cli.test.js
```

## Where to start

1. `bin/pinch.js` - the verb `switch` and `usage()`.
2. `test/tools.test.js` - the existing spawn style.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: chore: add an issue-template chooser and a short PR template
items.body:
## Context

GitHub only shows an issue chooser when `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` exists, so the community profile still reports `issue_template: None`. `pull_request_template` is also `None`.

## What to change

- Add `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` with three contact links: where to start, the private security path, discussions.
- Add `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` with three questions: what/why, does it touch a guard rail, and test+audit output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config.yml` parses as YAML
- [ ] Security link points at the private path in `SECURITY.md`, not a public form
- [ ] PR template is short enough not to add friction to a repo that already gates on 256 tests
- [ ] `community/profile` health reaches 100 after merge

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml'))"
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/RANJITHROSAN17/Pinch/community/profile | grep health_percentage
```

## Where to start

1. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` for the header style.
2. `SECURITY.md` for the reporting URL.

## Time estimate

~1 hour.

items.title: chore: prepare package.json for npm publish as pinch-ai
items.body:
## Context

The only install path is `git clone`. `npm i -g pinch` resolves to an unrelated 2022 package, so the product name is unavailable on npm; `pinch-ai` is free.

## What to change

- `package.json`: `private: false`, `files` allowlist, `main`/`exports`, `publishConfig.access: public`.
- `.npmignore` must exclude `data/`, `test/`, and `.env` explicitly.
- `README.md`: offer `npx pinch-ai setup` as the first install path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` tarball contains no `data/`, no `.env`, no `test/`
- [ ] Tarball under 1 MB
- [ ] `npx` path documented and tested from a clean directory

## How to verify

```bash
npm pack --dry-run
npm pack && tar -tzf pinch-ai-*.tgz | grep -E '^(package/data|package/test|package/\.env)' && echo LEAK || echo clean
```

## Where to start

1. `package.json`
2. `.gitignore` for the ignore patterns already known to be sensitive.

## Time estimate

~2 hours.
